TBe Khasi and Jalntia Hills hold the unique position of being a frontier of the ’^ominioa of India, as tbeir southern boundary impinges on East Pakistan. Tbe irdepenous people inhabiting these Hills are ent lely different from the rest of India as they have d.stinct traditions, culture and civili- sation of their own. From time immemorial, the area was ruled by Indegeiious democratic rulers called '‘Syiem”, ‘‘LyngdoLs” and “Sirdars”, elected by the people and subject to deposition by the vote of the people Ti e rulers are not hereditary, as when one dies or vacate his post the vacancy as a rule is filled up by election. The British entered into treaties and engage* ments with these States as semi-indeperdent States. Under the Brit;sh the Khtsis enjojed all tbe.r ancient rights and trJvileges and their democratic institutions were not interfe ed vitb. One of these privileges enjoyed by the people is, that they, and not their riders of their States are th^ owners of the land Sir Ke’th C mtl'e who has intimate koow- ledge of. tt^e Khasi people, having been incharjce of the area for a long period of years, in his authoritative book “Notes on Khasi Laws” quoting from a judgement of Colonel Bivar passed as early as 187 writes as follows “It is to be observed that the Chiefs in the Kbpsl Hills States are not territorial sovereign but elected democratic Chiefs and that they 48 have no right whatsoever to the soil, lands In theKhasi Hills, belonging to the chll^en of the soil, are the property of the owner, for right to wluch he is answerable to no Chief and for which he pays no land tax of what* ever nature and the only person who own demand re:t for land Is the proprietor who does as he thinks fit with his own and Is subject to no control in respect of it. A chief Is not a zamindar, he is, as I have said before, a democrat'c ruler and as such his power extends to the subject and not to the soil ” Unfortunately during the British regime, some Khasi Villages were allowed to secede from their parent States and to declaie themselves ts British are^s. On the eve of India’s Independence the Khasi rulers formed themselves into a Federation, and severally and jointly signed the Instrument of Ac- cession to tbe Dominion of India. One of the terms of this Instrument is that the seceded villages, should be allowed to rejoin their parent States.
